trajectory_summary: The call opens cold with a legitimacy challenge, warms substantially through the middle third as the rep uses the property lookup and home-size compliments to draw out real customer curiosity (backyard panels, net metering, referrals), but the back half stalls on a bill-collection dead end and ends without a locked appointment. The energy the rep built in the middle was not converted into a firm next step.
outcome_dispute: The call never produces a booked or tentative appointment with a specialist — it ends on a vague 'touch base tomorrow' after the customer failed to access his utility account. This should be tagged as a callback outcome, not booked or tentative, since no day/time for a specialist meeting was ever set.

observed_outcome.reasoning: No day or time was ever set for a specialist appointment; the call ends with a vague mutual plan to touch base 'tomorrow' after the customer attempts to get his utility bill data, which is a callback, not a booked or tentative appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: I would assume somewhere $200 or probably per your experience.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The $200 figure is explicitly the customer's own rough guess ('I would assume somewhere $200'), not a verified bill amount, and the rep never treats it as usable — instead the call moves to deferring actual bill/usage collection to a callback after the customer tries to get his utility's kWh history. This should be read as no real bill capture occurred on this call.

Yeah. 100%.') rather than tying it back to the value of getting on the calendar with a specialist.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: unanchored soft exit / no locked next step
primary_coaching_focus.quote: And then I'll just, once you're able to get that, if, you can just let me know or I can give you a call and then we can set up a meeting.
primary_coaching_focus.why: Despite strong mid-call engagement and a genuinely warm customer, the call ends with zero locked time, day, or commitment — just a mutual 'we'll see.' This is the single biggest value leak on an otherwise promising call and directly threatens whether this lead converts to any appointment at all.

key_moments.stewart_read: Second time the same liability concern surfaces, and the rep repeats the identical deferral without acknowledging the repetition or reassuring the customer that this is a normal, well-covered scenario.

The rep confirms the roof-only constraint but doesn't flag this as a strong buying signal for the specialist.
